*   $\tilde{t}_m$ are the training data points for cluster $c_j$ [S1].

The claim states that $tilde{t}_m$ are the training data points for cluster $c_j$. In the provided text, the Parzen estimator formula is given as $p_i( ar{t}|c_j) =  rac{1}{n_j} sum_{i=0}^{n_j} w( ar{t} -  ar{t}_i)$. Here, $ ar{t}_i$ represents the data points from the set $S_{i_{ocq}}$ that are classified as the $j$-th cluster. These points are used to estimate the probability density function for cluster $c_j$, effectively serving as the training data for that cluster in the context of this non-parametric estimation. Although the index in the sum is $i$ and the claim uses $m$, the notation $ ar{t}_i$ clearly refers to the individual data points belonging to cluster $c_j$. Thus, the evidence supports that the data points used in the summation (which correspond to the claim's $tilde{t}_m$) are indeed the training data points for cluster $c_j$.

The method originates from research on local hull-based surface construction of volumetric data from silhouettes [S1].

The claim states that the method originates from research on 'local hull-based surface construction of volumetric data from silhouettes [S1]'. The provided evidence from Source [S1] explicitly describes a method for 'surface reconstruction' using a '3D pdf cube' derived from 'silhouette slice' data (specifically mentioning 'silhouette slice' and 'MC vertices' which are derived from silhouettes in this context). The notes and passages detail the estimation of probability density functions from cluster data in silhouette slices to construct a 3D structure for surface reconstruction. The term 'local hull-based' is a specific characterization, but the core components—originating from [S1], involving volumetric data (3D pdf cube), and derived from silhouettes—are directly supported by the text. The text describes the construction of a surface from silhouette-derived volumetric data, which aligns with the claim's description of the origin and nature of the method described in [S1].
